title: Linkability of User Activities Over Time
description: GPS traces and timestamps in sensor batches allow linking user activities across different sessions, enabling tracking of movement patterns and behavior over time.
assumptions: Data is transmitted without anonymization or aggregation.

title: Direct Identification via Device ID
description: Transmission of unique device ID enables direct identification of the user, potentially linking data to a specific individual.
assumptions: Device ID is unique and not pseudonymized.

title: Eavesdropping on Data in Transit
description: Unencrypted transmission of sensor data between wearable and app could allow interception of sensitive information like GPS traces.

title: Insecure Data Storage at Destination
description: Companion app may store synced sensor data without adequate protection, risking unauthorized access to exercise/GPS data.
assumptions: App lacks encryption or access controls for stored data.

title: Lack of User Awareness About Data Collection
description: Users may not be informed that their sensor data (e.g., GPS, exercise sessions) is being synced to the app.
assumptions: No clear privacy notices or consent mechanisms.

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Laws
description: App's handling of synced data may violate regulations (e.g., GDPR) if data is processed without legal basis or user consent.
assumptions: App lacks compliance measures for data processing.
uncertainty_note: Node Nc.1.1 is a general assumption; specific regulation applicability may vary.

title: Linking location data with other health data
description: P3 combines location history from DS2 with other health data, enabling tracking of individuals across contexts and time.
assumptions: P3 has access to additional health datasets beyond location history.

title: Re-identification from location patterns
description: Location history stored in DS2 may allow re-identification of individuals through unique movement patterns, even if anonymized.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to enable re-identification.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of movement patterns
description: Derived daily routines and movement patterns from DS2 data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties via P3's outputs.
assumptions: P3 shares or exposes analytics results without proper access controls.

title: Lack of user transparency
description: Users may not be informed that their location data is used for analytics, violating informed consent principles.
assumptions: No clear user notification or consent mechanism exists for this data flow.

title: Violation of data protection regulations
description: Processing location data for analytics may not comply with GDPR or similar laws requiring purpose limitation and data minimization.
assumptions: Legal basis for processing is not established or documented.

title: Unauthorized Access to Sensitive Health Inferences
description: The app dashboard displays inferred health conditions (e.g., eating disorder or diabetes risk) to the user. If the app lacks adequate security controls (e.g., device authentication, encryption), unauthorized parties could access this sensitive data via the user's device.
assumptions: The app does not enforce strong access controls on the user's device.

title: Lack of Transparency in Data Processing for Inferences
description: Users may not be fully informed about how their data is processed to generate health risk inferences displayed on the dashboard, leading to uninformed consent or unexpected data usage.
assumptions: The app does not clearly disclose the purpose and methods of data processing for generating health inferences.
